summary: Yasuo Yuasa (1925–2005) was a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1973) under Tetsuro Watsuji. He held academic posts at Tokyo, Yamanashi, Osaka, and Tsukuba (1981–1989), later becoming Professor Emeritus at J. F. Oberlin University.

Yasuro Abe (b. 1953) works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Wako and Otani universities. His career includes posts at Osaka, Otemae, Nagoya (professor 1998, emeritus 2000–2019), the International Research Center for Japanese Studies, and Ryukoku University.

Yasushi Endo works in Indology and philosophy. He held positions at Nagoya University, International Buddhist University (attested as professor in 2000), and Aichi Bunkyo University (attested as lecturer 2000–2004).

Yasutaka Muroya works in Indology and philosophy. He served as a project research associate at the University of Vienna (attested 2007) and Leipzig University (attested 2015), and as a research associate at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (2016–2022).

Yasutoshi Murakami (b. 1941) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1960–1970). He held posts at Yamaguchi University (~1978–2004) and Koyasan University (~2004–2011), and served as president of the Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies (attested 2004).
Yawen Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).

Yellava Subbarayalu (b. 1940) specializes in Indology and history and archaeology. He served as a professor at Tamil University and worked as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (attested 2015).

Yeshe Thubten (1935–1984) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sera Monastery under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Geshe Rabten, Trijang Rinpoche, and Zong Rinpoche. He taught at UC Santa Cruz (1977–1978) and the University of Virginia (~1979–1980).
Yeshe Thupten works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1982, he held positions at Middlebury College and as a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia.

Yeshi Dhonden (1927–2019) was a specialist in Tibetology. He studied at the Chakpori Institute of Tibetan Medicine under Khyenrab Norbu. He founded the Men-Tsee-Khang in 1961, serving as its director from 1961 to 1966.
Yi-hsun Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Paul Groner.

Yifa (b. 1959) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at National Taiwan University, University of Hawaiʻi, and Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. She was a department head and dean at University of the West (~1996–2003) and a visiting scholar at Harvard.

Yigal Bronner is an Indology scholar who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1989–1994) and the University of Chicago (~1994–1999) under Sheldon Pollock. He held an academic post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~2010).

Yijie Tang (1927–2014) was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University (~1947–1951), where he later served as professor (~1956–2014), and also held a post at Stanford University (~1990–1991).

Yiliang Zhou (1913–2001) worked in history, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied at Fu Jen, Yenching (under Yinke Chen), and Harvard universities. He was a professor at Peking University from ~1952 to 1998.

Yin Shun (1906–2005) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Qingnian and Taixu, later earning a doctorate from Taisho University. He held leadership and teaching posts at Minnan, Wuchang, Sino-Tibetan, and Fawang Buddhist institutes, and headed the Hong Kong Buddhist Association.

Ying-shih Yü (1930–2021) was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Yenching, CUHK/New Asia College, and Harvard (PhD 1962). He held professorships at Michigan, Harvard, CUHK, Yale (1977–1987), Princeton (1987–2001), and Cornell, and was a fellow at Academia Sinica.

Yingguang Qu (1883–1973) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Hangzhou Chicheng Public School and received traditional training under Nordan Hutuktu, Nona Hutuktu, Bai Puren, and Gangkar Rinpoche.

Yinke Chen (1890–1969) was a scholar of sinology, history, and linguistics. He studied widely, including at Berlin, Zurich, Sciences Po, and Harvard. His academic posts included professorships at Tsinghua, Peking, National Southwestern Associated, Hong Kong, Yenching, and Sun Yat-sen universities.
Yirmiyahu Yovel (1935–2018) was a philosophy scholar. He was educated at the Hebrew Reali School, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1957–1968), and Princeton University (~1966–1968).
